upstream.description: A 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 running inference on a single CPU in 8.24 GB of RAM. Portable C99: no BLAS, no framework, no GPU.

classification.analysis: kimi-k3-in-c is a from-scratch, dependency-free C99 inference engine that runs the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 mixture-of-experts model on a single CPU using only 8.24 GB of peak RAM, by streaming the 1.56 TB checkpoint's routed experts from disk (never resident) while keeping a small dense trunk in memory with an LRU expert cache. It uses AVX2/FMA SIMD kernels, MXFP4 quantization, and techniques like KDA linear attention and MLA to make an enormous MoE model runnable on ordinary consumer hardware (laptop to workstation) with byte-identical output regardless of RAM budget, only trading off speed. Aimed at systems programmers and ML engineers interested in low-level, zero-framework LLM inference engineering; extensively documented with benchmarks, architecture diagrams, and a test-gated build (make test) that validates against a PyTorch reference.

use_cases.title: Run a 2.78T-parameter model locally on a laptop with just 8GB RAM
Study a from-scratch C99 transformer/MoE inference engine implementation
Learn how expert streaming and LRU caching make huge MoE models fit in limited memory
